output.brief:
The latency regression is not caused by gateway 5.8. It comes from the storage compaction tuning change (FC-7710) pushed the evening of 2 Nov. That change raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Disk use went from 41% to 97% and disk read waits rose from 9 to 205 ms, and node-side GET time rose from 61 to 262 ms. Every cell that received the change went over 150 ms within minutes of the push, whatever gateway version it ran. The one cell that skipped the change (aps-3) is still at about 94 ms even though it runs 5.8. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. Network and overall traffic growth don't explain it. The 5.8 rollout and the config push just happened to overlap, and the config push isn't on the change calendar, which hid it.

Do not roll back the gateway. It would not fix latency and would reopen the security hole. Do not pause compaction, because the backlog would then climb past 15% and risk full disks. Revert FC-7710 in one cell first, watch p99 and backlog, then extend the revert to the other cells. Hold off on limiting Orrin's ingest until the 10 Nov attribution job shows where the backlog came from. Confidence is high on the cause and moderate on the backlog source.
